name: The Temporal Equivalence Principle: Suppressed Density Scaling in Globular Cluster Pulsars
description: Gravitational time dilation in General Relativity is confirmed to 10⁻⁵ precision in the Solar System. At intermediate astrophysical scales, however, persistent anomalies emerge. The Temporal Equivalence Principle (TEP) formalizes an alternative: that time dilation is scale-dependent. This work reports a 5.8σ–7.7σ dynamical anomaly in globular cluster pulsar timing that challenges standard density scaling (4.1σ tension). Analysis of 394 millisecond pulsars (196 GC, 198 field) reveals a 0.59 dex excess in spin-down magnitude—cluster pulsars spin down faster than field controls. The signal exhibits Suppressed Density Scaling (Slope 0.39 ± 0.08 vs Newtonian ~0.72), saturating in dense cores. Complementary analysis of gravitational lensing places upper limits on cosmological temporal shear (|Γ| ≤ 104 days/decade), which rules out runaway modifications but remains consistent with the screened parameters suggested by pulsars.
